sourceIssues.correction: Replace finite by countable. A dense countable subset meets each open coset, so the quotient is countable and the group is sigma-compact.
sourceIssues.reason: The self-dual group Z×R/Z is separable and has compact-open subgroup{0}×R/Z with quotientZ. Finiteness is false; countability proves exactly what is needed.

sourceIssues.printed: Own-word paraphrase, not a source quotation: The coefficient estimate is printed without absolute values and its finite-polynomial maximum is signed.
sourceIssues.correction: Use |a_d| and max|e_d|, with E positive; keep the same exponent and support.
sourceIssues.reason: Theorem8.2 needs absolute convergence of signed coefficient sums. The exact head coefficients alternate signs, so a one-sided bound cannot justify the interchange.
sourceIssues.known: The downloaded latest arXiv copy retains the omission; no separate correction located.

sourceIssues.locator: BKLPR arXiv1304.3971v2, proof of Theorem5.16, pp.23–24; author final copy Theorem5.17 proof, pp.25–26
sourceIssues.printed: Own-word paraphrase, not a source quotation: The upper harmonic estimate is used with coefficient1/2 although the preceding lemma only gives upper coefficient2.
sourceIssues.correction: Use numerator≤2ε logN+O(logM) and denominator≥(1/2)logN; the limsup is at most4ε and still tends to0.
sourceIssues.reason: Weights of square-order groups lie between1/N and2/N. The lower constant cannot also be used as an upper bound. Only a fixed multiple of ε is needed.
sourceIssues.known: The author final copy retains the stronger constant; no separate correction located.

sourceIssues.locator: BS5 arXiv1312.7859v1, Proposition40 proof, equation(33), p.29
sourceIssues.printed: Own-word paraphrase, not a source quotation: A joint linear constraint is asserted after replacing the two conditional means by their separate limsups.
sourceIssues.correction: Derive the needed bound for the total mean at each finite height, using the same odd/even counts and the lower bound on the odd mean, then pass to the limsup. Use the corresponding finite count argument for lower-density estimates.
sourceIssues.reason: Separate limsups can occur along different subsequences. For a toy example let (a_n,b_n) alternate(1,0),(0,1): every a_n+b_n=1 but limsup a_n+limsup b_n=2. The finite empirical inequalities prove the target constants without this invalid operation.
sourceIssues.known: No correction located in the version read; the result survives this elementary repair.
searched: Source equations compared with the direct finite-height derivation in this packet

sourceIssues.locator: BKLOS arXiv1709.09790v2, Theorem2.2 and Section9 proof, pp.3,12–13; author PDF same locators
sourceIssues.printed: Own-word paraphrase, not a source quotation: For O=Z[ψ] of Z-rank t and #O/ψ=3^e the proof asserts a lower bound3^((e/t)rank A_s(F)) on the ψ-index for every twist.
sourceIssues.correction: Retain the unrestricted claim as a gap. Add an explicit uniform positive rank-index hypothesis, or specialize to ψ=[3], where the free Z-module calculation gives the bound with c=1.
sourceIssues.reason: For a product with ψ=(id,[3]) the degree3 chain can operate solely on the second factor; its Selmer groups and ψ-index give no control on the first factor’s Mordell–Weil rank. Even O=Z[(3,9)] has unequal component index rates, so arbitrary O-modules do not have the uniform e/t rate. No counterexample to the broader average-rank conclusion is claimed.
sourceIssues.known: No correction located; the abstract states the sound[3] specialization, but the theorem and Section9 in the author PDF retain the broader claim.
searched: arXiv1709.09790 abstract and version history (latest v2)
